messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: auth.introspect.errors > 25% across prod-us-east and prod-eu with sustained 429s starting 13:02 UTC. Paging @oncall-sre.

oncall-sre: I’m on it, joining call in 2 mins. digging into rate-limit headers now.

emma (prod-eng): seeing 429 + 502 mixed. token-verifier svc logs show bursts of `HTTP/1.1 429` from Okta introspect and timeouts on retry. sample log: `introspect okta token_id=abc123 status=429 retry_after=10`

raj (platform): Okta status page shows degraded auth service in `us-east-1` with increased rate-limiting: https://status.okta.com/incident/xyz :confused:

okta-status-bot: Confirmed: Okta reported higher-than-normal request volume, mitigation in progress; ETA unknown.

alex (eng): Early customer reports: SSO login failing on web console, 500s and stuck spinner. Support queue spiking.

sophie (support): Can confirm, several customers on paid tiers affected. Triage: affected flows are new login & session revalidation; existing sessions still fine.

oncall-sre: Mitigation plan: 1) throttle our fanout to Okta from token-verifier (reduce concurrency from 100 -> 20). 2) Enable local session cache TTL bump for 5m to reduce introspect traffic. 3) Add exponential backoff and failfast for repeated 429s. Implementing now.

emma (prod-eng): Pushing quick patch to token-verifier: set `MAX_CONCURRENCY=20` and enable `CACHE_TTL_OVERRIDE=300` for session cache. Rolling to prod-us-east first.

alex (eng): Deploy snippet:
```
kubectl set env deploy/token-verifier MAX_CONCURRENCY=20 CACHE_TTL_OVERRIDE=300
kubectl rollout restart deploy/token-verifier -n prod
```

oncall-sre: Also toggling internal-only permissive auth for console in prod-us-east for SRE/admins to unblock investigations: config change `console.auth.strict=false` for SRE group only.

raj (platform): Pushed Gateway rule to reduce parallel introspects: `gate.authz.max_parallel_introspects=20` and set `gate.authz.fail_open=false` (we'll fail closed but rely on cached sessions).

okta-status-bot: Okta indicates rate limits are tied to token introspect endpoints; they advise reducing request rate and leverage caching.

emma (prod-eng): After throttling and cache bump, we see introspect requests drop ~70% from token-verifier in us-east. Error rate down from 27% -> 6% in 7 mins.

alex (eng): Partial customer impact remains: new logins still ~3% failure for some geos. Support: please use workaround doc to guide affected customers (session refresh, retry after 30s).

sophie (support): Noted, sending canned response to affected customers and flagging priority accounts. Will update ticket numbers in the incident channel.

oncall-sre: Action item: open high-priority support case with Okta, include request-id samples and our mitigation steps. @raj pls attach logs and rate-limit headers.

raj (platform): Case created: OKTA-INC-12345. Attached sample headers:
```
x-rate-limit-limit: 200
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
retry-after: 10
```

emma (prod-eng): Also enabling short-term gate rule to coalesce identical introspect requests (prefix dedupe) to avoid fanout storms for same token. Patching token-proxy layer now.

alex (eng): Observability: added temporary dashboard showing introspect qps, 429/502s, cache hit rate, and customer success rate. Linking here: https://dashboards.internal/redwood/auth-introspect-spike

oncall-sre: Timeline so far: 13:02 alert -> 13:06 throttle in place -> 13:12 cache bump -> 13:18 dedupe rollout -> 13:22 error rate improved. Current status: degraded but stabilizing.

sophie (support): Customer impact estimate: ~3% of new logins failed during peak (13:02-13:25) across multi-tenant pool. No data plane loss besides console auth.

emma (prod-eng): Risk: if Okta doesn't finish mitigation we should consider temporary fallback to short-lived internal JWT verification for low-risk internal flows, but that requires emergency config and audit. Need signoff from security.

oncall-sre: Noted - security approval required. @raj escalate to security and SOC for quick review.

raj (platform): Looping security: `@security` we propose short-term fallback: accept our internally minted session tokens for console read-only access for SRE/admins only. Will capture audit logs. Approve?

(okay, security channel ack happened off-thread)

oncall-sre: Handoff plan for next oncall: summarizing current state and outstanding items.

- Incident root: Okta introspect rate-limiting causing token verification errors and login failures.
- Mitigations applied: concurrency throttling, cache TTL bump, request dedupe/coalescing, conservative console permissive mode for SRE, added dashboards, Okta support case OKTA-INC-12345.
- Impact: ~3% new-login failures for ~20 minutes peak window, admin console limited for some users.
- Next actions: 1) monitor Okta status and our error rate dashboards for 2 hours, 2) coordinate Okta support replies, 3) roll back permissive console when stable, 4) write postmortem and add long-term fix: token cache warmers and better backpressure at edge.

oncall-sre: Paging next oncall for 13:30 UTC handoff: @emma (prod-eng) take over incident commander, @raj owns platform fixes, @sophie holds customer comms.

emma (prod-eng): I'll take incident comms and follow Okta case. Dropping into handoff meeting in 3.

alex (eng): Quick note for postmortem: add synthetic test to detect introspect 429s earlier and an automated throttling policy to avoid sudden fanout.

sophie (support): I’ll compile affected customer list and follow up with account teams.

okta-status-bot: Okta updated status: mitigation underway; request volume decreasing.

oncall-sre: Closing slack thread for now — handoff complete to @emma. Will update incident channel with final resolution and postmortem link when ready. :white_check_mark:

emma (prod-eng): Final note for handoff: timeline + runbook entry to be added to /wiki/incidents/authz-fanout and postmortem draft will be ready by EOD.
